newsitem.title: CHINA: Mongolia Jan-Nov trade surplus plunges to $4.6 mln.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia Jan-Nov trade surplus plunges to $4.6 mln.

text.p: Mongolia registered a foreign trade surplus of about $4.6 million in January-November, down drastically from $79.7 million in the same period a year ago, the State Statistics Centre said on Tuesday.
Mongolia had imported $380.6 million worth of goods in the 11 months this year, compared to $344.95 million last year, the centre said in a report.
Exports were $385.2 million in the period, down from $424.6 million in 1995, the centre said.
The largest proportion of the country's imports came from Russia, with Mongolia purchasing $130.7 million worth of Russian goods in the period, it said.
Imports of Japanese goods totalled $61.5 million while those from China were $57.6 million, it said.
Switzerland was the biggest buyer of Mongolian export items at $95.8 million, followed by Russia with $82.6 million and China with $66 million, it said.
The main Mongolian exports continued to be copper and cashmere while imports were largely petroleum and petroleum products, it said.
